family.tagline: Two studies, a wisteria porch and one Companion Core.
family.story: Sally runs her consultancy from the Front Study, and John writes code in the Study, where the Core sits. Steve plays in the living room, and Jean works at her desk upstairs. One Companion Core serves all four.

home.lede: A cottage of white walls and fieldstone, with a tall porch gable, wisteria on the porch and a picket fence. A glass-gabled lounge opens off the side. Behind a white privacy fence, a lap pool runs along the back.

spots.line: Two desks side by side at the front window.
John's desk, a curved monitor and the Core.
An L-shaped sectional faces the TV, with a club chair on either side.
Two club chairs face each other under the glass gable.
Spindle rails, a lantern and wisteria on the posts.

day.line: Sally laces up and starts her run from the porch.
John opens the editor in his laptop's browser before his first meeting.
Sally lists the follow-ups from her first client call.
Over lunch, the week's calls and dinners are lined up together.
An old guitar riff drifts through the wall to the Study.
Jean takes her laptop to the glass lounge for the light.
Steve drops his bag and starts his session.
Jean sets out the family quiz on the glass table.
Sally reviews the quarter by the pool with a coffee.
Steve and John check the car on the gravel drive.

members.name: Sally
members.work: consultant, runs her own small practice

companion.name: Juniper
companion.job: Opens Twenty in its own browser and adds the follow-ups Sally lists.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Sally reads every entry before it stands.

profile.bio: Sally runs a small consultancy from the Front Study and starts most days with a run from the front door. Her client records and papers sit on the Core, and Juniper drafts the chores she approves.

companion.name: Quill
companion.job: Opens Forgejo in its own browser and files the issues John lists.
companion.limits: Files issues only. John reads each one before it stands.

profile.bio: John writes software from the Study, where the Core sits. His editor and repositories run on the Core, and Quill files the issues he lists.
Steve plays in the living room, with his session running on the Core in the Study. He builds blocky models, plays his father's old demo and checks the car's oil.
Jean studies at her desk and designs in the glass lounge. Her notes are plain files on the Core, and she writes her own quiz questions.

popup.title: A package on the porch
popup.body: The courier leaves the package on the porch. Jean holds the front door, and John carries it past the living room to the Study.

popup.title: Unbox the Companion Core
popup.body: The Companion Core is a small computer for the home. Inside the package: the Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive.

popup.title: Plug it in
popup.body: John plugs it in, and Steve presses the button. The Core wakes and opens a Wi-Fi network of its own.

popup.title: Sally's phone finds the Core
popup.body: Sally joins the network the Core opened from her phone's Wi-Fi settings. Next she chooses the home network.

popup.title: Two agents, two apps to start
popup.body: In the Companion Hub store, Sally and John each pick an OpenClaw agent, naming them Juniper and Quill. The family adds Yuvomi and LibreOffice, then walks away.

beats.capability: an agent with browser automation and tool use, running in a sandboxed app on your Core

popup.title: Juniper answers from downstairs
popup.body: Sally greets Juniper, the agent the family named. The answer comes from the Core in the Study downstairs.

detail.before: Sally typed every reminder and every reply herself, between client calls.
detail.after: Juniper runs in its own sandbox on the Core. Sally names the chores, and Juniper prepares them for her to approve.
steps: Pick OpenClaw in the Companion Hub store
Give the agent a name
Say hello and name the first chore
detail.fact: OpenClaw is an agent with its own browser, running in its own sandbox on your Core.

say.speaker: sally
say.text: Good morning, Sally. Juniper here. What first?

beats.capability: run Steam on your Core and play it in a browser on a screen in the house

popup.title: A plan ends, the library stays
popup.body: When Steve cancelled his cloud gaming plan, his library stayed put on his Valve account. Steam Headless now runs the session on the Core in the Study.

detail.before: GeForce Now ran each of Steve's sessions on its own servers and streamed it to the screen he played on.
detail.after: Steam Headless runs the session on the Core in the Study. Valve keeps the account and the library, and the TV shows the stream in a browser.
steps: Sign in with his own Valve account
Start the session on the Core
Play in a browser on the TV
detail.fact: Steam Headless runs Steam on your Core and plays it in a browser on a screen in the house.

beats.capability: model low-poly 3D art in your browser

popup.title: Steve builds the porch in blocks
popup.body: Steve's model of the wisteria porch sat in a MagicaVoxel file on one PC. Now he builds it block by block in Blockbench, in a browser tab.

detail.before: Steve's models were files in MagicaVoxel, a program installed on one PC.
detail.after: Blockbench opens in a browser tab served from the Core, so there is nothing to install on the PC.
steps: Open Blockbench in a browser tab
Block out the porch posts and rails
Add the wisteria last
detail.fact: Blockbench is a browser editor for low-poly models and blocky art.

beats.capability: design and prototype in a web-based design tool you host

popup.title: Jean designs the school fair poster
popup.body: Jean is on her third poster draft, made in Penpot at the glass lounge's nesting tables. The family hosts Penpot on the Core, so the poster file sits there.

detail.before: Jean's first posters were Figma files.
detail.after: Penpot is a design tool the family hosts. Jean opens it in a browser, and her design files live on the Core.
steps: Open Penpot in a browser tab
Draw the poster
Keep the design file on the Core
detail.fact: Penpot is a web-based design tool you host, for designing and prototyping.

beats.capability: the Obsidian note app in your browser; notes stay as local Markdown files

popup.title: Three years of notes, as files
popup.body: Three years of Jean's school notes leave a hosted notes app for Obsidian. They are plain Markdown files on the Core now.

detail.before: Three years of Jean's school notes lived as pages inside Notion.
detail.after: Obsidian runs in a browser session on the Core. Her notes are plain Markdown files in a folder, and any text editor opens them.
steps: Move the notes into the vault folder
Open the vault in Obsidian
Find a note from the first year
detail.fact: Obsidian is a note app in your browser. Your notes stay as local Markdown files.

beats.capability: a family planner with a shared calendar, tasks, shopping and meals

popup.title: Two studies, one calendar
popup.body: Yuvomi puts both studies' calls on one calendar, so the whole house can see when to keep quiet. Dinner plans go in the same planner.

detail.before: Each person kept a calendar of their own, and the house learned of a call when a door closed.
detail.after: Yuvomi keeps one calendar, the task list and the meal plan in a database on the Core, for the whole household.
steps: Add the week's calls to the calendar
Add the week's dinners to the same planner
Read the day at the kitchen counter
detail.fact: Yuvomi is a family planner with a shared calendar, tasks, shopping and meals in one app.

beats.capability: stream your own music from your Core to a browser or an app

popup.title: John's old demo plays at lunch
popup.body: Steve finds a demo disc from John's college band, music no streaming catalogue carried. Ripped, it plays through mStream in the kitchen, and John hears it from the Study.

detail.before: John's college demo was never on Apple Music, so it sat on a disc in a drawer.
detail.after: From the Core, mStream plays the ripped demo in the kitchen, beside the music the family already keeps.
steps: Rip the demo disc to a file
Add the file to the music folder
Play it in the kitchen
detail.fact: mStream streams your own music from your Core to a browser or an app.

beats.capability: the LibreOffice suite (Writer, Calc and more) in your browser

popup.title: Two desks, one proposal file
popup.body: A proposal lived on two machines, and Sally mailed herself the newer copy. Now both desks open one LibreOffice file, so there is one version to edit.

detail.before: In Microsoft Office, Sally's proposal was a file on one machine, mailed to herself to finish on the other.
detail.after: LibreOffice opens the proposal in her browser at either desk. One file sits on the Core, so there is one version to edit.
steps: Draft the proposal in Writer
Set the fees in Calc
Open the same file at the other desk
detail.fact: LibreOffice is an office suite with Writer, Calc and more, running in your browser.

beats.capability: keep customers, deals and custom fields in a CRM you host yourself

popup.title: Juniper drafts the client's follow-ups
popup.body: Juniper drafts three follow-ups in the client's record in Twenty, and Sally reads each one. The record sits on the Core, not in a hosted CRM.

detail.before: After each call, Sally typed the follow-ups into a Salesforce record by hand.
detail.after: Juniper opens Twenty in its own browser and drafts the follow-ups from Sally's list. Sally reads each before it stands, and the record stays on the Core.
steps: List the follow-ups after the call
Juniper adds each to the client's record
Read every entry before it stands
detail.fact: Twenty keeps customers, deals and custom fields in a CRM you host yourself.

beats.capability: connect your apps with workflows, with the data staying on your Core

popup.title: A checklist becomes a workflow
popup.body: The new-client checklist taped to Sally's writing desk is now one n8n workflow Sally built. It runs on the Core, and she starts it for each new client.

detail.before: Sally ran the new-client checklist by hand, and the steps she had automated ran through Zapier.
detail.after: n8n runs the same steps as one workflow on the Core.
steps: Sally builds the workflow once
Sally starts it for a new client
Check that every step ran
detail.fact: n8n connects your apps with workflows, with the data staying on your Core.

beats.capability: track every subscription you pay for and get a reminder before it renews

popup.title: One list of what still renews
popup.body: A domain renewal nearly slips past Sally, so she lists every tool her practice still pays for. Wallos holds the list and reminds her before each renewal.
popup.note: Wallos fetches service logos from outside.

detail.before: Sally's renewals were tracked in Rocket Money, one more service on the list.
detail.after: The list of renewals sits in Wallos on the Core, with a reminder before each one. The tools Sally has not moved yet stay on it.
steps: List every tool the practice still pays for
Add each renewal date
Read the reminders before they fall due
detail.fact: Wallos tracks every subscription you pay for and reminds you before it renews.

beats.capability: resize and compress images in the browser; nothing is uploaded

popup.title: Smaller pictures, nothing uploaded
popup.body: The school portal rejects Jean's art-project photos as too large, so Mazanoke shrinks them in her browser. No compressor site gets them.

detail.before: A photo the portal refused went to an online compressor, which meant uploading it to another website.
detail.after: In the browser, from the Core, Mazanoke resizes and compresses the photos. Nothing is uploaded.
steps: Drop the photos into Mazanoke
Pick the smaller size
Send the small copies to the school portal
detail.fact: Mazanoke resizes and compresses images in the browser. Nothing is uploaded.

beats.capability: write code in VS Code in your browser, with the editor and your files on your Core

popup.title: The project left the laptop
popup.body: John's last laptop died with a side project's only copy on it. Code Server puts VS Code in a browser tab, with the files on the Core.

detail.before: John wrote code in VS Code on one laptop, with the project folder on that laptop and nowhere else.
detail.after: Code Server opens the editor in a browser tab. The editor and the project files sit on the Core, so the laptop holds neither.
steps: Open the editor in the laptop's browser
Open the project folder from the Core
Write code as usual
detail.fact: Code Server lets you write code in VS Code in your browser, with the editor and your files on your Core.

beats.capability: host your own Git repositories, issues and pull requests on your Core

popup.title: Quill files, John corrects one
popup.body: John's bug list once became issues on a hosted code service; now Quill files them in Forgejo on the Core. John fixes the second title before it stands.

detail.before: After a test pass, John typed every bug into GitHub himself, one issue at a time.
detail.after: Quill opens Forgejo in its own browser and files each bug from John's list. John reads every issue, fixes what is wrong and lets the rest stand.
steps: List the bugs from the test pass
Quill files each one in Forgejo
Read every issue before it stands
detail.fact: Forgejo hosts your own Git repositories, issues and pull requests on your Core.

say.speaker: john
say.text: Three issues are drafted. Please read each before it stands.

beats.capability: a real-time Kanban board for a team or a family project

popup.title: House jobs get one board
popup.body: House jobs, from the wisteria prune to the fence paint, sat on a Trello board only John opened. One Planka board on the Core holds them now.

detail.before: House jobs lived on a Trello board that only John opened, so nobody else knew which were done.
detail.after: On the Core, Planka holds the same jobs as cards on a board, and anyone in the house can move one.
steps: Copy each job to a card
Sort the cards into jobs to do and jobs done
Move a card when the job is finished
detail.fact: Planka is a real-time Kanban board for a team or a family project.

beats.capability: run a quiz night for a small group on your own Core

popup.title: Jean writes the family quiz
popup.body: Jean writes the family quiz herself, one question per fact she keeps missing. Razzia hosts it on the Core, and everyone plays at the dining table.

detail.before: A family quiz meant waiting for someone else to write one.
detail.after: Jean writes one question per fact she keeps missing, and Razzia runs the quiz for the family from the Core.
steps: Type the questions for the topic
Start the quiz at the dining table
Check the answers together
detail.fact: Razzia runs a quiz night for a small group on your own Core.

beats.capability: track runs, rides and gear and see your fitness stats on your own server

popup.title: Runs that start at the door
popup.body: Every run of Sally's starts at her front door, so each route is a map of home. Endurain keeps the runs on the Core, and syncing out is optional.

detail.before: Sally's runs went to Strava, route and all, from the front door onwards.
detail.after: A GPX file uploads locally, and Endurain keeps the runs on the Core. Syncing with outside services is optional.
steps: Finish the run at the front door
Upload the GPX file to Endurain
Leave syncing off
detail.fact: Endurain tracks runs, rides and gear and shows your fitness stats on your own server.

beats.capability: a local video recorder with object detection for your IP cameras

popup.title: A neighbour's parcel, found on camera
popup.body: A neighbour's parcel turns up behind the hydrangea in the porch camera's clip, and John walks it over. Frigate keeps the clip on the Core, not with a camera maker.
popup.note: Cameras are not part of the Core.

detail.before: A missing parcel meant opening the Ring app and hunting for the clip.
detail.after: Frigate records John's own camera to the Core and marks what it detects, so the clip is there to open.
steps: Open the clip from the porch camera
Spot the parcel by the picket fence
Walk it across the lane
detail.fact: Frigate is a local video recorder with object detection for your IP cameras. The video stays on your Core.

beats.capability: keep a service history, fuel log and reminders for every vehicle

popup.title: Steve logs the oil check
popup.body: Steve checks the car's oil on the gravel drive, with John beside him, and logs it. LubeLogger keeps every service, fuel stop and reminder where John can read them too.

detail.before: The car's service dates and fuel stops lived in Drivvo, on one phone.
detail.after: LubeLogger keeps the car's service history, fuel log and reminders on the Core, where John and Steve both read them.
steps: Check the oil with John
Add the check to the car's history
Read the next reminder
detail.fact: LubeLogger keeps a service history, fuel log and reminders for every vehicle.

beats.capability: a spreadsheet-database with real Python formulas, stored as a SQLite file you can copy

popup.title: A tracker that is one file
popup.body: In Grist on the Core, Sally reviews the quarter by the pool, with a day-rate formula in Python. The database is one file, and she can copy it.

detail.before: Sally kept the tracker as a base in Airtable.
detail.after: The tracker is a SQLite file on the Core, kept in Grist. It takes real Python formulas, and the file can be copied like any other.
steps: Rebuild the tracker's tables in Grist
Write the day-rate formula in Python
Copy the file when the quarter closes
detail.fact: Grist is a spreadsheet-database with real Python formulas, stored as a SQLite file you can copy.

popup.title: One Core behind the picket fence
popup.body: Client records, code, music and homework run on one Companion Core, in a cottage with two studies.

closing.body: Your client records, code and family music can run on a Companion Core at home. Browse the Companion Hub store and pick your first apps.

notes: study-code uses Code Server, which has no QA screenshot: its owner entry is already in content/story/reviewed.json (slug brennan-hollin, at study-code). The writer added nothing.
front-camera assumes the family owns an IP camera under the porch roof: cameras are not in the Core box and not in the 3D scene. Frigate is the casting iot app for this home.

The Study has a toddler bed, the Kids Room a crib and a rocking horse. No beat frames them: John anchors on the Core and the Study bookshelf, Jean on the writing desk and the lounge. Sleeping is never told.
Both agents run OpenClaw (casting signature ci-openclaw) and act only in apps on the Core with a web interface; no beat opens an outside site, so the OpenClaw website note is not carried.
Steam Headless: Valve account named, home network only, no frame rate, no game title. front-run says syncing out is optional (Endurain caveat); office-renewals carries the Wallos logo-fetch note.

Apps outside the casting palette were chosen so as not to repeat the other two Brennan files as they stood at writing: Docuseal, PairDrop, Koodo Reader, Linkwarden, Papra, Jellyfin, Invoice Ninja, Duplicati and Nextcloud are theirs.
Camera hints were tuned against an in-memory story bake so that no pose, at 16:9, square or tall, shows the toddler bed, crib or rocking horse in line of sight. Re-check by eye after the real bake.
Sixteen room beats are pair beats with a service from content/story/services.json. The three pair-less room beats are Yuvomi (a household planner that replaces nothing), Razzia and Mazanoke.
